newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS-Vedior shines on Amsterdam bourse debut.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Vedior shines on Amsterdam bourse debut.

text.p: Shares in employment services group Vedior NV began trading on the Amsterdam bourse at 48.00 guilders each on Thursday, far outstripping the issue price of 39.00 guilders a share and market expectations.

Dealers and analysts had expected the shares in the group, around 20 percent of which is currently being floated by majority shareholder Vendex International, to open at around 44.00 to 45.00 guilders.
"An opening of nine guilders above the issue price is quite something, I think it will push many smaller players to just take their profits to spend a nice week-end," one dealer said.
The issue price had been set at 39.00 guilders, below the upper side of the price range, although Vendex said the subscription had been some 30 times oversubscribed.

Last Thursday, Vendex said strong demand from both retail and institutional investors, and the increase in share prices of international services companies had lead the company to revise the issue price range of Vedior shares.
The range for the flotation was upped to 37-40 guilders from 33-37 guilders.
"With the issue 30 times oversubscribed, you can see the higher range finally did not have a major impact," a dealer said.
"And by setting the price at 39.00 guilders, Vendex put some water into the wine, showing it didn't really want to overexploit the demand," he added.

Market sentiment toward the offshoot of business and retail group Vendex is positive, although dealers and analysts said the stock did not merit the same valuation as Dutch number one in the sector, Randstad.

"The entire sector is flourishing and sentiment toward it is very positive. (Dutch temp organization) Start released very healthy figures and good prospects yesterday, in line with those of foreign players," another dealer said.
He saw great possibilities if the upswing in the French market persisted, but added Vedior's margins were likely to remain lower than Randstad's.
Fernand de Boer, analyst at SNS Securities said Vedior shares seemed to have good growth potential, but added he expected Vedior to remain relatively cheaper than Randstad.

"There's a lot of interest in the stock and Vedior has set ambitious goals. Margins can be improved... but I have my doubts they can attain their goal of a 20 percent market share, notably in the Netherlands," he said.
He said a five to six point discount in the price/earnings ratio to Randstad seemed reasonable. Randstad trades on a price/earnings ratio of around 43.
"Vedior and Randstad can't be compared. Randstad has a very solid market position in the Netherlands, and it has proven itself much more than Vedior," he said.
Dealers foresee a good start for Vedior on the Amsterdam exchange, after which the stock's performance might level off.
"Many (institutional) parties will want to have a reasonable position in that stock, so there are a lot of buyers at the beginning of trade," one dealer said.
"On the future I am more conservative, I think the stock will move in line with the market," another dealer said.
Vendex is issuing some 16.7 million Vedior shares in its flotation and is likely to offer an additional 2.5 million shares through a "greenshoe" option.
The share price faded to 45.70 guilders at 1147 GMT with 2.9 million shares changing hands.
